answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Entry needs court clerk service record: hearings clerked at one court across years of sittings. The price is per head, and the hollow test proves it: The cost lands per head: 566 aliases need 566 records, each checked live against the issuer, so bulk forgery costs 566 times what one honest seat costs. The island trail is public, the dawn check is cheap to run, and a farm of 566 aliases pays 566 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
